decision: The protocol step requires adding 0.1 mL (100 µL) of buffer to the sample tube. The initial lab state shows the sample tube and buffer are in the fridge, which is closed. The expected lab state requires the fridge closed and items returned. Available APIs include fridge.open, fridge.close, robot.pick, robot.place, tube.uncap, tube.cap, pipette.attach_tip, pipette.transfer, pipette.discard_tip, etc. The workflow must: open fridge, pick buffer and sample tube (or just move them to bench), uncap tubes, attach pipette tip, transfer buffer, cap tubes, place items back, close fridge. All required APIs are registered. The final state should match expected: fridge closed, items in fridge, pipette no tip.
reasoning_summary: Plan: 1) Open fridge. 2) Pick buffer from fridge to bench. 3) Pick sample tube from fridge to bench. 4) Uncap sample tube. 5) Uncap buffer (assuming it's a tube). 6) Attach pipette tip. 7) Transfer 100 µL from buffer to sample tube. 8) Cap sample tube. 9) Cap buffer. 10) Place buffer back to fridge. 11) Place sample tube back to fridge. 12) Discard pipette tip. 13) Close fridge. All APIs are in available_apis, so no unregistered APIs.
assumptions: Buffer is treated as a tube with tube_id 'buffer' for uncap/cap operations, though in lab_state it's a reagent. This is a simplification to use available APIs.
The robot.pick/place operations are used to move items between fridge and bench, assuming 'bench' is a valid location string.
